reason: The PR replaces the Nogood propagator's per-nogood predicate vectors with an arena allocator, aiming to remove double indirection and repeated allocations in the solver engine.
solver_behavior_hypothesis: Contiguous nogood storage may reduce propagation overhead in conflict-heavy runs, but the default one-gigabyte preallocation could increase peak memory and hurt small instances.
workload_exposure_plan: Use exact CP instances that learn and revisit nogoods; record conflicts, propagation work, solve time, and peak memory for matched base and PR builds.
mathematical_risk: Incorrect arena indexing or stale nogood references could miss valid propagation, prune feasible assignments, or produce a false infeasibility claim.
independent_check_plan: Check satisfying assignments against original constraints and compare satisfiable and unsatisfiable statuses with an independent CP or SAT solver on tractable instances.
hidden_generalization_plan: Use paired hidden instances from distinct CP model families and sizes under the same time and memory limits, retaining OOM and timeout outcomes.
overlap_review: The PR body identifies related PR #209 on a different branch; compare the two source diffs and count only a non-overlapping historical task lineage.
causal_chain: Arena-backed predicate storage removes per-nogood allocation and double indirection during propagation; the default large preallocation may instead raise memory pressure.
structural_trigger: Constraint-programming instances that learn and revisit nogoods during exact search.
activation_probe: Count learned nogoods, propagator visits, allocator growth, and peak RSS on both source states.
instance_selection_rule: Freeze CP model families with and without learned-nogood pressure before hidden outcomes; retain OOM and timeout cases.
resource_risk: The PR defaults to roughly one gigabyte of preallocated predicate storage and may exceed task memory limits.
